quotes.quote: a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.
Lazarus was one of those who sat at the table with him.

stages.text: Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.

payload.name: Crowd in John
payload.note: Large crowds who follow Jesus, are fed at the five thousand and debate his identity in John's gospel.

stages.label: Crowd in John

quotes.quote: So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him.

stages.text: Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.

payload.title: Saul's vision on the road to Damascus

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: the men with Saul
payload.note: Men traveling with Saul to Damascus who hear the voice but see no one.

stages.label: Travelling companion of Saul
stages.text: The men with Saul: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, lean build from road travel; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beard; plain, weathered faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic with a brown wool travelling cloak in dusty earth tones. Carries a walking staff and a leather satchel.

payload.name: Damascus
payload.note: Capital city of Syria, seat of Ben-hadad and Rezon, and home of Naaman's rivers, judged in Amos and linked with Paul's conversion and escape in Acts and 2 Corinthians; all entries here are the same city.

stages.label: Damascus

quotes.quote: synagogues of Damascus
the rivers of Damascus
guarded the Damascenes’ city
went up against Damascus and took it

stages.text: Damascus: a walled oasis city of pale limestone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs and domes, set against arid hills; date palms, orchards and irrigated gardens watered by the rivers Abanah and Pharpar; a city gate with a wall, and a straight main street lined with walls and shaded arcades.

payload.title: Creation groans and the Spirit's intercession
Way to Golgotha; the crucifixion

payload.name: Simon of Cyrene
payload.note: Cyrenian man compelled to carry Jesus' cross; the father of Alexander and Rufus in Mark; distinct from every other Simon in the group.

stages.label: Simon of Cyrene

quotes.quote: Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus
coming from the country

stages.text: Simon of Cyrene: a man in his forties, sturdy and broad-shouldered from years of field labour; olive-brown skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and a close-cropped beard streaked with grey; a lined, steady face with deep-set dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist, with a rough brown wool cloak thrown over the shoulders, dusty from the road. No signature props.

payload.name: The Roman soldiers
payload.note: Roman soldiers (and Herodian soldiers in Luke) who mock, crucify and guard Jesus across all three Gospels; they are one body of soldiers seen from different accounts, so all three entries describe the same group.

stages.label: The Roman soldiers

quotes.quote: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

stages.text: The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.

payload.name: Golgotha
payload.note: The hill outside Jerusalem called the place of a skull, where Jesus is crucified; the Matthew and John entries describe the same place and join here.

stages.label: Golgotha

quotes.quote: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
When they came to the place that is called “The Skull”
He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”

stages.text: Golgotha: a rounded rocky knoll of pale limestone rising just outside the walls of Jerusalem, bare of trees and scrub except for thin dry grass in cracks. Its crown is worn smooth and bony-white, giving the hill its name, the place of a skull. A rough stone-cut quarry face and a few low olive trees stand at its foot, and the walls and towers of the city rise distant behind it.

payload.title: Living creatures and the elders worship

payload.name: John the seer (Revelation)
payload.note: Author and visionary on Patmos who receives and records the revelation; the narrator of Revelation, distinct from other Johns.

stages.label: John the seer

quotes.quote: to his servant, John
I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression

stages.text: John the seer: man of about sixty, of middle height and spare build, weathered olive skin from exile by the sea, short greying hair and a close grey beard, lined brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a rough dark brown wool mantle. He carries a worn wooden staff and a small scroll case.

aliases: the creature with a face like a man
payload.name: Four living creatures (Revelation)
payload.note: The creatures around God's throne in Revelation, full of eyes, who worship God and call forth the four horsemen; distinguished from the Ezekiel beings by their role at the throne and the seals.

stages.label: Four living creatures

quotes.quote: each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within
as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes

stages.text: Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Robes of deep crimson and white.

payload.name: Twenty-four elders of Revelation
payload.note: Twenty-four elders seated on thrones around God's throne, clothed in white with golden crowns.

stages.label: Twenty-four elders of Revelation

quotes.quote: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne
each one having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense
These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they

stages.text: Twenty-four elders: mature men of venerable age, grey or white-bearded, of dignified and grounded build; skin warm olive-brown; hair white and worn to the shoulder, full white beard; calm, noble faces. Signature outfit: long white robes with gold sashes and a golden crown on the head. Props, carried alone: a golden harp or a golden bowl of incense.

aliases: the sea of glass before the throne
payload.name: Heavenly throne room
payload.note: The heavenly court of God in Revelation, with the throne, elders, living creatures, the Lamb and the sea of glass before the throne.

stages.label: Heavenly throne room

quotes.quote: there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne
the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened
Lightnings, sounds, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail followed.

stages.text: Heavenly throne room: a vast open sanctuary of radiance beneath a heaven like crystal, floored with a sea of glass that is clear as crystal, set with a great throne and a temple whose doors open onto the heavens, lit by lightnings, thunders and a rainbow the colour of emerald about the throne. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.

payload.title: New heaven and new earth

payload.name: New Jerusalem
payload.note: Holy city descending from heaven with twelve gates (Revelation).

stages.label: New Jerusalem

quotes.quote: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God
out of the holy city, which are written in this book

stages.text: New Jerusalem: a great and high city descending out of heaven, luminous and pure as crystal, its walls of jasper set on twelve foundations adorned with precious stones, and twelve gates of pearl. Its streets are pure gold, clear as glass, with no temple and no sun or moon, lit by the glory of God. Beside it flows a river of life, clear as crystal, and on its banks stands the tree of life bearing fruit each month.

payload.title: Battle with Amalek; Moses' hands raised

payload.name: Hur
payload.note: Companion who holds up Moses' hands during the battle with Amalek and is left with Aaron to oversee disputes.

stages.label: Hur

quotes.quote: Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side.

stages.text: Hur: man in his fifties to sixties, sturdy and weathered from desert travel; medium build with strong, steady arms; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark hair and a trimmed grey beard; calm, dignified face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain woven undertunic of undyed cream linen under a rust-brown wool cloak. No props.

payload.name: Amalekites
payload.note: The Amalekite people, an enemy nation that attacks Israel at Rephidim in Exodus, comes against Israel at Hormah in Numbers, and is recalled in Deuteronomy as the nation that struck Israel's weary rear; all three refer to the same people.

stages.label: Amalekites

quotes.quote: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Amalekites: a typical warrior of a desert people, adult, aged roughly twenty-five to forty; lean, weathered build; sun-darkened olive-brown skin; dark hair tied back, short beard kept close; strong, wind-creased face with a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic belted with leather, over it a sand-coloured woven cloak in ochre and brown. Carries a curved sword at the belt and a leather shield as their own props.

payload.name: Rephidim
payload.note: Camp in Exodus where Israel struck the rock for water at Massah and Meribah and fought Amalek; the rock and battle story are specific to this site.

stages.label: Rephidim

quotes.quote: encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.

stages.text: Rephidim: a wide, dry valley of pale sand and broken limestone in the Sinai wilderness, bordered by low, rust-coloured cliffs. A single great rock face of dark grey granite rises at the valley's head, its surface cracked and streaked with mineral stains. Sparse thorn scrub and tufts of dry grass grow in the gullies, with a few stunted acacia trees near the rock. Distant peaks of Sinai show as blue-grey shapes on the horizon.

payload.title: Water from the rock at Meribah
Peter denies Jesus

payload.name: Crowd in Luke
payload.note: The mass of people following Jesus, hearing John and being healed throughout Luke.

stages.label: Crowd in Luke

quotes.quote: a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon
A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

stages.text: Crowd in Luke: a typical member is an ordinary adult of Judean or Galilean village life, from young adult to middle age, lean and sun-worn, with olive or brown skin, dark hair kept short or tied back, and a short beard or clean-shaven face; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, undyed cream and earth brown, with a woollen cloak and a head covering; carries no props of their own.

aliases: the court of the high priest
the courtyard of the high priest
payload.name: the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)
payload.note: Courtyard of Caiaphas where Jesus is tried and Peter denies him in Matthew; same court as the high priest's court in John, identified by Caiaphas and the trial setting.

stages.label: The court of the high priest

quotes.quote: the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas
He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest

stages.text: The court of the high priest: an open paved courtyard of pale limestone flagstones inside a high-walled stone house in Jerusalem. A wide arched gateway with a timber door faces the street. A charcoal fire burns on a stone hearth at the centre of the court, and a stone porch with columns stands along one side. Olive and fig trees grow in clay pots by the walls; the upper walls are plastered and lit by torch sconces.

payload.title: Healing of the lame man at the temple gate

payload.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: the Jerusalem temple
payload.note: The single Jerusalem temple building across all five divisions (courts, porch and gates are parts of the same place), so every entry is one place.

stages.label: The Jerusalem temple

quotes.quote: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
the door of the temple which is called Beautiful
how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts
His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

stages.text: The Jerusalem temple: a vast complex of white limestone and gleaming gold on a raised stone platform atop Mount Moriah. Wide colonnaded courts, a tall sanctuary house with a gilded roof, a great curtained veil within, a treasury chamber, and a Beautiful Gate of bronze. Olive trees and cedar frame the courts.

payload.title: Samuel anoints David at Bethlehem

payload.name: Samuel
payload.note: Son of Hannah raised at Shiloh, judge and prophet who anoints Saul and David; the child of Eli's temple, not Elkanah.

stages.label: Samuel as a boy at Shiloh

quotes.quote: The child was young.
The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.

stages.text: Samuel: a boy of about ten years, slight and sturdy, with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair and clear, attentive eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of pale ochre with a short linen ephod-style sash, bare feet. He carries no props.

stages.label: Samuel as judge and prophet

quotes.quote: Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
Fill your horn with oil, and go.
Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

stages.text: Samuel: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with weathered brown skin, a close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, short hair and calm, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a deep blue wool cloak. He carries a horn of oil at his belt and, on journeys, a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Jesse
payload.note: Bethlehemite father of David and his seven sons.

stages.label: Jesse

quotes.quote: The man was an elderly old man in the days of Saul.
I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite

stages.text: Jesse: an elderly man of Bethlehem in Judah, past sixty, lean and upright from years of labour; olive-brown skin weathered by sun; short grey beard close to the jaw; grey hair under a plain head-cloth; deep lines around the eyes and a steady, serious face. Signature outfit: an undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark brown woollen cloak with a thick fringe at the hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of dark wood; no other props alone.

payload.name: Eliab
payload.note: Eldest son of Jesse, David's oldest brother, who is angry at him in the valley of Elah.

stages.label: Eliab, firstborn son of Jesse

quotes.quote: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle
Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men

stages.text: Eliab: man in his twenties, tall and broad-shouldered from years of shepherding and soldiering; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a trimmed beard; strong brow, straight nose and a set, stern mouth. Signature outfit: a sleeveless tunic of undyed linen under a rust-red cloak, with bronze scale armor on the shoulders. Carries a round bronze shield and a short sword.

payload.name: Abinadab son of Jesse
payload.note: Jesse's second son passed over by Samuel at Bethlehem; distinct from the Kiriath Jearim host who keeps the ark.

stages.label: Abinadab son of Jesse
stages.text: Abinadab son of Jesse: man in his twenties; sturdy, broad-shouldered build; olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and short beard; steady, serious face with a strong nose. Signature outfit: undyed linen tunic with a plain blue-grey wool cloak. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Shammah
payload.note: Son of Jesse passed over by Samuel; serves in Saul's army.

stages.label: Shammah

quotes.quote: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by.
the third Shammah

stages.text: Shammah: a young man of about twenty, lean and sinewy from shepherding and soldiering; medium height; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard; calm, steady features with a serious, dignified bearing. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep ochre woollen cloak. Signature prop: a leather sling.

payload.name: Ramah of Benjamin (Ramathaim Zophim)
payload.note: Home city of Elkanah, Samuel's birthplace and seat of judgment in 1 Samuel; not the Baasha border town, and identified by the Samuel sections and the Ramathaim Zophim alias.

stages.label: Ramah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim
he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to Yahweh there
came to the great well that is in Secu
under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Ramah of Benjamin: a hill town on a rocky ridge in the hill country, terraced slopes of olive and terebinth, low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and fieldstone, a stone altar of unhewn stones set on the high ground, a great well with a worn stone rim near the town's edge, a tamarisk tree standing in the open, and a little sanctuary of Naioth on the rise.

payload.title: David offers to fight Goliath

payload.name: Gibeah of Saul (1 Samuel)
payload.note: Saul's home town and royal seat in 1 Samuel, where Saul is found, anointed and later fights the Philistines at Michmash; distinguish from the Judges Gibeah by its link to Saul and the monarchy.

stages.label: Gibeah of Saul

quotes.quote: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah
under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron
Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Gibeah of Saul: a fortified hill town of Benjamin on a rocky ridge in the central highlands. Stone-walled terraces climb the slopes, flat-roofed houses of limestone and mudbrick cluster near a citadel tower at the crest, and a town gate faces the approach road. Terebinth and pomegranate trees grow at the edge of the upper town, with a tamarisk tree in the open ground below, and hills of scrub and olive fall away eastward toward the wilderness.

payload.title: Saul's jealousy and spear

payload.name: the evil spirit from God
payload.note: Spirit that troubles Saul and is eased by David's harp.

stages.label: The evil spirit from God

quotes.quote: Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will be well.

stages.text: The evil spirit from God: no body or face, shown only as a dark, heavy shadow gathering about Saul's chamber, a cold wind that stirs the hangings and dims the lamplight, its edges sombre grey and bruised violet, faintly threaded with a dull ember glow.

payload.title: Daniel rebukes Belshazzar

payload.name: Belshazzar
payload.note: King of Babylon during the feast and handwriting on the wall; slain the same night.

stages.label: Belshazzar, king of Babylon

quotes.quote: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords
his face was changed in him

stages.text: Belshazzar: a man in his thirties or early forties, of lean, upright build; olive-bronze skin; short dark hair and a neatly curled beard in the Mesopotamian royal manner; a strong brow and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long fringed royal robe of deep crimson wool over a white linen tunic, with a tall, pleated, gold-banded crown. Carries a gold-hilted ceremonial dagger at the belt.

payload.name: Royal palace of Babylon
payload.note: Babylonian palace where the king receives counsel, sees the handwriting and hears Daniel's interpretations; distinct from the Susa palace.

stages.label: Royal palace of Babylon

quotes.quote: he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon

stages.text: Royal palace of Babylon: a vast walled complex on the flat alluvial plain of the Euphrates, built of sun-dried and fired brick glazed in deep blue with yellow lion and dragon reliefs. Tiered terraces rise toward a great gate with tall towers; hanging gardens of palms, date trees and climbing vines spill over the walls. Broad courts of pale stone lead to a banquet hall with high cedar-beamed ceilings and a river-facing colonnade.

payload.title: Hosea's marriage and the naming of his children

payload.name: Hosea
payload.note: Son of Beeri, prophet to Israel who marries Gomer and buys back an adulterous wife.

stages.label: Hosea

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word that came to Hosea the son of Beeri
Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of unfaithfulness

stages.text: Hosea: man in his late thirties to forties; lean, weathered build from years of travel; olive skin darkened by sun; short dark hair and a close-cropped beard streaked with early grey; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow. Wears a plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a earth-brown cloak with a fringed hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of dark olive wood.

payload.name: Gomer
payload.note: Daughter of Diblaim and wife of Hosea, the adulterous wife in the prophet's marriage sign.

stages.label: Gomer

quotes.quote: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived, and bore him a son.

stages.text: Gomer: a woman of about twenty-five to thirty; slender, medium build; olive skin darkened by sun; long dark hair bound up under a plain linen head-veil; soft, weary features with a serious mouth and wide dark eyes. Signature outfit: an undyed or ochre-brown linen tunic with a dark wool cloak in faded indigo. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Jezreel
payload.note: Firstborn son of Hosea and Gomer, named as a sign of the bloodshed of Jehu's house; an infant only.

stages.label: Jezreel, infant son of Hosea

quotes.quote: Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while

stages.text: Jezreel: an infant of a few months, small and soft-limbed, with dark curling hair and warm olive-brown skin of an Israelite village child. Round face, dark eyes, small rounded features. Wears a plain undyed linen wrap or small tunic in natural cream with a simple woven band at the waist. Carries no props.

payload.name: Lo-Ruhamah
payload.note: Daughter of Hosea and Gomer, named as a sign that Yahweh will no longer pity Israel; an infant only.

stages.label: Lo-Ruhamah, infant daughter of Hosea

quotes.quote: she conceived again, and bore a daughter. Then he said to him, “Call her name Lo-Ruhamah
Now when she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she conceived, and bore a son.

stages.text: Lo-Ruhamah: an infant girl of a few months to two years, small and soft-limbed; warm olive-brown skin of the Israelite hill country; fine dark hair, tufted and short, unbound; round face with large dark eyes and a small mouth; wrapped in a plain undyed linen swaddling cloth with a faded blue-grey wool covering. Carries no props.

payload.name: Lo-Ammi
payload.note: Second son of Hosea and Gomer, named as a sign of Israel's rejection; an infant only.

stages.label: Lo-Ammi, infant son

quotes.quote: Call his name Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.

stages.text: Lo-Ammi: an infant of a few months, small and soft-limbed, with dark wisps of hair. Olive-brown skin of the Levant, round cheeks, and dark eyes. Wrapped in a plain undyed linen swaddling cloth, with a simple cream-coloured tunic beneath.

payload.name: Hosea's house
payload.note: Home of Hosea and Gomer where the marriage and children are placed.

stages.label: Hosea's house
stages.text: Hosea's house: a modest two-room dwelling of mud-brick on a low stone footing, flat roof of packed earth and beaten reed, a courtyard of trodden clay with a clay oven and grinding stone, low walls of rough fieldstone, a single doorway facing a dirt lane, olive tree and terebinth beside it, dry hillside vineyards and terraces beyond, muted ochre and grey tones.

payload.name: Jezreel
payload.note: The city of Jezreel in the Israelite kingdom, the royal city of Ahab and Jezebel where Naboth's vineyard lay and where Jehu executed the royal house; the same city appears in Samuel, Kings and Hosea, with the valley of Jezreel named in Hosea.

stages.label: Jezreel

quotes.quote: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which was in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.
the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel
the Israelites encamped by the spring which is in Jezreel.

stages.text: Jezreel: a walled royal city on a low ridge at the edge of a broad green valley, fed by a spring at its foot. Mudbrick and fieldstone houses rise in terraces; a palace of cut stone and cedar beams stands beside a walled vineyard of terraced vines and olive trees. A rampart of packed earth and stone encircles the town, with a gate and a stone watchtower on the wall.

payload.title: Asa's alliance with Ben Hadad and Hanani's rebuke

payload.name: Asa, king of Judah
payload.note: Son of Abijah and king of Judah who removes idols and makes a treaty with Ben Hadad of Syria against Baasha; the same king appears in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, so both entries belong to one cluster.

stages.label: Asa, king of Judah

quotes.quote: in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet
Asa was diseased in his feet. His disease was exceedingly great

stages.text: Asa: man of mature years, lean and upright, in his forties to sixties; olive-brown skin; short dark beard with grey at the chin; black hair bound back under a plain linen headband; lined, earnest face with steady dark eyes; wears an undyed linen tunic and a deep blue wool royal cloak fastened at the shoulder with a bronze pin. Carries a plain staff of almond wood, a sign of age and his later infirmity.

aliases: Ben Hadad the king of Syria
payload.name: Ben Hadad, king of Syria (son of Tabrimmon)
payload.note: King of Syria at Damascus who makes treaties and wars with Israel and Judah in Kings and Chronicles, including the alliance with Asa; the Ben Hadad of Kings and Chronicles are the same king.

stages.label: Ben Hadad, king of Syria

quotes.quote: Ben Hadad the king of Syria gathered all his army together
Ben Hadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions
Ben Hadad fled and came into the city, into an inner room.

stages.text: Ben Hadad: a mature man in his late forties, broad-shouldered and strong, olive-bronze skin. Short dark curled beard trimmed close, hair bound back under a royal fillet. Stern, weathered face with a hooked nose and heavy brows. Signature outfit: a long embroidered tunic of deep crimson under a dark blue court robe with gold trim. Signature prop: a short gold-hilted sword at his belt.

payload.name: Hanani the seer
payload.note: Prophetic seer in 2 Chronicles who rebukes King Asa for trusting Syria and is imprisoned; distinct from Nehemiah's brother of the same name.

stages.label: Hanani the seer

quotes.quote: Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah

stages.text: Hanani the seer: man in his fifties to sixties; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; long grey-streaked hair and full beard; lined, grave face with steady eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak. Carries a worn wooden staff.

payload.title: Eliphaz on the fate of the wicked

payload.name: Eliphaz the Temanite
payload.note: Oldest of Job's three friends, from Teman; first to speak in the dialogues and recounts a night vision.

stages.label: Eliphaz the Temanite

quotes.quote: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite

stages.text: Eliphaz the Temanite: a man of about sixty, lean and upright; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; short grey-streaked beard trimmed close; deep-set, thoughtful eyes and a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a dark russet wool cloak. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.title: Jew and the law, true circumcision
Prayer for guidance and forgiveness
Righteousness by faith and the Gospel for Israel
Proverbs of Solomon copied by Hezekiah's men

aliases: the men who copied these proverbs
payload.name: Men of Hezekiah
payload.note: Court scribes of King Hezekiah who copied the proverbs of chapters 25 to 29; act only as copyists.

stages.label: Men of Hezekiah

quotes.quote: which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

stages.text: Men of Hezekiah: a typical scribe of the Judean royal court, aged thirty to fifty; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a trimmed beard; calm, attentive face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark indigo wool cloak; a leather belt. Signature prop: a wooden writing board with a reed pen and an ink pot at the belt.

payload.name: The king's court
payload.note: The royal court in Proverbs where kings sit on thrones and princes and officials attend; a human court, not the heavenly assembly in Job.

stages.label: The king's court

quotes.quote: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;

stages.text: The king's court: a broad, stone-paved hall within a royal palace of dressed limestone and cedar beams, its high throne of ivory and gold raised on a few steps at the far end. Walls hung with embroidered linen in deep purple and blue, and tall bronze-capped pillars along the sides. Lamps of olive oil and low, dignified light. Palace gates of stone nearby.

payload.title: Marriage as an image of Christ and the assembly
Boy Jesus in the temple

payload.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
payload.note: Virgin mother of Jesus, betrothed to Joseph of Nazareth; appears in the nativity, the wedding at Cana, the cross, and the upper room. Distinct from Mary Magdalene and Mary of Bethany.

stages.label: Mary, mother of Jesus

quotes.quote: to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
But standing by Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

stages.text: Mary: a young woman of about fifteen to twenty-five years; slender, of medium height and modest build; olive skin of a Galilean Jewish woman; dark brown hair worn covered beneath a veil; calm, deep-set dark eyes and a grave, gentle face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a long blue-grey wrap-cloak drawn over her head and shoulders. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Joseph, husband of Mary
payload.note: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus from Nazareth, of David's line, a carpenter who receives angelic dreams; distinct from Joseph of Arimathea and the other Josephs in the work.

stages.label: Joseph, husband of Mary

quotes.quote: Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man
Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?
because he was of the house and family of David

stages.text: Joseph: a man of about thirty to forty years; a sturdy, working build with strong, calloused hands; olive-brown skin weathered by sun and work; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard with some early grey; a steady, careful, gentle face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown beneath a dark brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a carpenter's adze or wooden mallet carried at his belt.

payload.title: Hezekiah's Passover
Prophecy of the kings of north and south

aliases: a man in linen with a face like lightning
payload.name: Man clothed in linen (Daniel)
payload.note: The heavenly figure who appears to Daniel by the Hiddekel river and delivers prophecies of future kings and the end of days. Distinguished from Ezekiel's man in linen by the river vision and the prophecies to Daniel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen (Daniel)

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river
he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: an adult of ageless, powerful bearing; lean, broad-shouldered build; skin of pale bronze, glowing faintly; face like lightning, hair and beard close and bright as burnished gold; eyes like flaming torches; arms and legs like polished bronze. Signature outfit: a white linen garment girded at the loins with gold of Uphaz. Carries no props.

payload.name: the river Ulai
payload.note: River beside which Daniel sees visions; the great river Hiddekel in chapter 10.

stages.label: The river Ulai

quotes.quote: I was in the citadel of Susa, which is in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision, and I was by the river Ulai.

stages.text: The river Ulai: a broad, slow watercourse winding through the flat alluvial plain of Elam below the citadel of Susa. Its banks are packed brown clay, cut by reed-beds of tall pale reeds and tamarisk, with palm groves and willows standing back from the water. Mud-brick walls and baked-brick towers of the citadel rise on the high ground above, and the water runs clear and dark beneath the open sky.

payload.title: Teaching on retaliation
God's promise and the fate of the wicked
Jephthah's war and vow

payload.name: Jephthah
payload.note: Gileadite chief who vows his daughter as a burnt offering.

stages.label: Jephthah the Gileadite

quotes.quote: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor. He was the son of a prostitute.
Then Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob. Outlaws joined up with Jephthah

stages.text: Jephthah: a man in his middle years, strong and weathered from years of living as an outlaw in the land of Tob; lean, broad-shouldered build; olive-brown skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and a short, close-cut beard streaked with grey at the chin; a steady, serious face with deep lines at the eyes. Signature outfit: a dark brown woven wool cloak over an undyed linen tunic, belted with cord. Signature prop: a plain wooden war bow slung across the back.

payload.name: Jephthah's daughter
payload.note: Jephthah's only child who greets him with tambourines and is given up by his vow.

stages.label: Jephthah's daughter

quotes.quote: his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dances
She was his only child.

stages.text: Jephthah's daughter: young woman in her teens, slender, medium height; olive-brown skin; long dark hair worn loose or bound with a linen band; calm, open face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a woven linen tunic in undyed cream with a deep blue woven shawl over the shoulders. Carries a small hand tambourine of hide and wood.

payload.name: Elders of Gilead
payload.note: Gilead's elders who recall Jephthah and make him their head; distinct from the wider Israelite assembly.

stages.label: Elders of Gilead

quotes.quote: the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah out of the land of Tob.
the people made him head and chief over them.

stages.text: Elders of Gilead: a typical elder, men aged fifty to seventy, of sturdy build and weathered brown skin; close-trimmed grey-streaked beard and hair bound back; lined, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed wool with a deep indigo cloak. Carry no props.

aliases: king of the children of Ammon
payload.name: Ammonites
payload.note: Peoples oppressing Israel east of the Jordan and warring with Jephthah.

stages.label: Ammonites

quotes.quote: The king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah

stages.text: Ammonites: adult men and women of varied ages, typically middle-aged warriors; sturdy, broad-shouldered build; olive to warm brown skin; dark hair worn bound or short, men often with short-trimmed beards; strong, weathered facial features with no caricature; signature outfit a knee-length woven tunic in undyed linen under a dark wool cloak in ochre or deep red; carries a round shield and short sword as signature props.

payload.name: Tob
payload.note: Land where Jephthah lives with outlaws before he is recalled in Judges.

stages.label: Land of Tob

quotes.quote: Then Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob.
the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah out of the land of Tob.

stages.text: Land of Tob: rolling hill country east of the Jordan, wooded slopes of oak and terebinth, stony pasture and wadi beds, with scattered walled villages of mud brick and fieldstone, flat roofs, and watchtowers on high ground. Dry scrub and wild grasses; rocky outcrops and caves in the hills.

payload.name: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)
payload.note: The Gileadite gathering place in Judges where Jephthah speaks before Yahweh and the war against Ammon is organized; distinguished by the Judges setting and Gilead context.

stages.label: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)

quotes.quote: The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.
Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.

stages.text: Mizpah: a high ridge of pale limestone and red-brown earth in the hill country of Gilead, terraced for gathering. Flat open ground at its crest is ringed by low dry-stone walls and a few squat mud-brick and stone shrines with plain lintels. Scattered terebinth and oak stand at the edges, with olive groves and grey scrub on the slopes below.

payload.name: Minnith
payload.note: Places where Jephthah defeats the Ammonites with a great slaughter.

stages.label: Minnith

quotes.quote: He struck them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, even twenty cities

stages.text: Minnith: a fortified highland town on a rise above wheat fields and terraced vineyards, with thick mud-brick walls of pale ochre, a gate tower of dressed stone, and flat roofs. Olive and terebinth trees stand along the eastern slope, and a dry watercourse runs at its foot.

payload.title: Boaz shows kindness to Ruth

payload.name: Reapers of Boaz's field
payload.note: Boaz's harvest workers in Ruth's story, who are kind to Ruth while she gleans; not the laborers whose wages are withheld in James.

stages.label: Reapers of Boaz's field

quotes.quote: after the reapers
the young men have drawn

stages.text: Reapers of Boaz's field: young men and maidens in their late teens to twenties; lean, sun-browned, strong-handed workers of Israelite stock; olive to deep brown skin; dark hair tied back under a cloth, young men with short cropped hair and light stubble; open, calm faces. Signature outfit: undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a plain cloth girdle, sleeves pushed up, in earth brown and ochre. Props: a sickle of bronze or flint-set wood carried at the belt.

payload.name: Boaz's barley field
payload.note: Barley field in Bethlehem where Ruth gleans after the reapers, owned by Boaz; the field of the gleaning story.

stages.label: Boaz's barley field

quotes.quote: glean among the ears of grain
the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech
When you are thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink from that which the young men have drawn.

stages.text: Boaz's barley field: a broad, gently rising tract of open farmland on the hills near Bethlehem, its ground dry and pale gold after harvest. Ripe barley stands in uneven rows of ears, with stone field walls and a few terraced boundaries. Scattered olive and fig trees edge the far margins, and a well or water vessels stand near the reapers' side. Low stone village houses are visible at the distance.

payload.title: Consecration rituals for the priests and altar
The wisdom of God and the foolishness of the cross
Rejection of Saul and the death of Agag

payload.name: Agag
payload.note: Amalekite king spared by Saul and killed by Samuel at Gilgal.

stages.label: Agag, king of the Amalekites

quotes.quote: He took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive
Agag came to him cheerfully.

stages.text: Agag: a man of middle years, in his fifties, lean and upright with a sturdy build; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; dignified, proud features with deep-set eyes; wears a long undertunic of undyed wool and an indigo-blue court cloak edged in ochre, with a gold-banded leather belt; carries a curved bronze sword at his hip.

payload.name: Gilgal (Saul's coronation and rejection)
payload.note: Site in 1 Samuel where Saul is made king, offers sacrifice and is rebuked by Samuel.

stages.label: Gilgal

quotes.quote: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah
All the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Yahweh in Gilgal.

stages.text: Gilgal: a low, open limestone plateau in the Jordan valley near Jericho, with scattered grey standing stones and a rough stone altar of unhewn rock. Terebinth and tamarisk trees at its edges, dry grass, a few mud-brick and fieldstone houses on the rise. Bethel and Mizpah lie on the hills to the west.

payload.title: Craftsmen begin; the people give too much

payload.name: Bezalel
payload.note: Chief craftsman of Judah, son of Uri, who builds the tabernacle.

stages.label: Bezalel, craftsman of Judah

quotes.quote: Behold, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
in whom Yahweh has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary

stages.text: Bezalel: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sturdy from long labour with wood, stone and metal. Warm brown skin, dark hair cropped close, a short full beard flecked with grey. Calm, attentive face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain woven tunic of undyed linen under a wool cloak of deep blue, with a leather work apron. Carries a bronze chisel and a plumb line of cord.

payload.name: Oholiab
payload.note: Craftsman of Dan who assists Bezalel on the tabernacle.

stages.label: Oholiab

quotes.quote: an engraver, and a skillful workman, and an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen.

stages.text: Oholiab: man in his middle years, sturdy and deft-handed; medium build; warm brown skin; short dark hair and a close-cut beard greying at the chin; calm, attentive face with lines from years of close work. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a blue-violet woven cloak with a narrow scarlet border. Carries alone a bronze engraving burin on a leather cord.

payload.title: Catalogue of the journeys

payload.name: The plains of Moab (Numbers)
payload.note: The camp across the Jordan from Jericho, also called Shittim, where the second census, Balaam's oracles and the Baal Peor apostasy take place; distinguish from the Deuteronomy camp by the Numbers events and the Shittim/Jericho alias.

stages.label: The plains of Moab (Numbers)

quotes.quote: The children of Israel traveled, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
They traveled from the mountains of Abarim, and encamped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Israel stayed in Shittim;

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low, level tract of grey-green steppe east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, cut by the river's dense tamarisk and reed belt. Acacia (Shittim) groves and scrub grow on the plain; distant bluffs of the Abarim range rise eastward, and the walled city of Jericho glimmers across the river to the west. Scattered stone and mud-brick settlement walls, low tents of black goat hair, and open cairns mark the land.

payload.title: Run the race looking to Jesus
The burning house and the aftermath

aliases: the old man by the brazier
payload.name: Sherlock Holmes
payload.note: Consulting detective of Baker Street, Watson's friend and the investigator in every division of this group, who disguises himself variously; appears across all stories.

stages.label: Sherlock Holmes

quotes.quote: He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen
tweed-suited and respectable, as of old

stages.text: Sherlock Holmes: man in his thirties; lean, long-limbed, narrow-shouldered build; pale skin; dark hair kept short; clean-shaven face with a hawk-like nose, deep-set grey eyes and a sharp, watchful expression; wears a dark tweed suit with a waistcoat, a plain collar and a dark overcoat. Carries a clay pipe and a magnifying glass.

payload.name: Dr. Watson
payload.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion, a doctor and chronicler, present in every story of this group.

stages.label: Dr. Watson

quotes.quote: I think, Watson, that you have put on seven and a half pounds since I saw you.
I am lost without my Boswell.

stages.text: Dr. Watson: a man in his thirties, of solid, medium build, filled out somewhat since his marriage; fair skin, short brown hair parted neatly, a trimmed moustache, and a steady, open face. Wears a dark wool frock coat, grey waistcoat, white collar and dark tie, with a bowler or silk hat. Carries a physician's black bag.

payload.name: Victor Hatherley
payload.note: Young hydraulic engineer, orphan and bachelor, who arrives at Watson's consulting-room with a severed thumb and recounts his night at Eyford; the narrator's patient and Holmes' client.

stages.label: Victor Hatherley

quotes.quote: the other was so strange in its inception and so dramatic in its details
Mr. Victor Hatherley, hydraulic engineer, 16A, Victoria Street (3rd floor).

stages.text: Victor Hatherley: young man in his mid twenties; slight to middling build; fair skin, pale from strain; short light-brown hair parted neatly; clean-shaven with a fine, serious face; a bandaged left hand. Signature outfit: a dark grey wool frock coat over a waistcoat and white collar, the coat worn at the collar. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Inspector Bradstreet
payload.note: Scotland Yard inspector who accompanies Holmes and Hatherley to Eyford and studies the ordnance map.

stages.label: Inspector Bradstreet

quotes.quote: Inspector Bradstreet, of Scotland Yard, a plain-clothes man
Bradstreet had spread an ordnance map of the county out upon the seat and was busy with his compasses

stages.text: Inspector Bradstreet: man in his forties; sturdy, medium build; fair skin weathered by outdoor work; short greying-brown hair, neatly parted; clean-shaven apart from a trim moustache; alert grey eyes and a broad, good-humoured face. Signature outfit: a dark grey wool frock coat over a waistcoat, with a dark four-in-hand tie and a black bowler hat. Carries an ordnance map, brass compasses and a pencil.

payload.name: the station-master
payload.note: Station-master at Eyford who reports the fire at Dr. Becher's house.

stages.label: the station-master

quotes.quote: The station-master laughed heartily.
“Yes, sir!” said the station-master.

stages.text: The station-master: a stout, hearty man in his fifties, broad-shouldered and ruddy-cheeked from outdoor work, with clean-shaven jowls and short greying side-whiskers. Dark blue railway uniform coat with brass buttons and a peaked cap, a waistcoat beneath, and a watch chain across his belly. Carries a lantern and a railway timetable.

payload.name: Eyford Station
payload.note: Small village station near Eyford, Berkshire, where Hatherley arrives and later wakes.

stages.label: Eyford Station

quotes.quote: reached the little dim-lit station after eleven o’clock
As I passed out through the wicket gate
It is a good seven miles from Eyford Station.
a small clump of trees in the neighbourhood

stages.text: Eyford Station: a small rural station in Berkshire, a single short platform of old brick and timber under a plain pitched roof, with a low lamp post and a dim-lit waiting shelter. A wooden wicket gate opens onto a narrow lane. Surrounding country is flat, open fields and hedgerows of hawthorn, with scattered oaks and a dark clump of trees beyond. Nearby stands a quiet village of brick cottages.

payload.name: Eyford house
payload.note: The isolated whitewashed house near Eyford in Berkshire where the press is, which later burns down.

stages.label: Eyford house

quotes.quote: the bumping of the road was exchanged for the crisp smoothness of a gravel-drive
a porch which gaped in front of us
It was pitch dark inside the house

stages.text: Eyford house: an isolated two-storey rural house of whitewashed brick set back from a country road, reached by a smooth gravel drive. A deep porch shelters the front door, opening onto a dark hall and a long passage with rooms off it. Sash windows, slate roof, a few bare trees and rough hedgerows surround it, with flat fields of farmland beyond.

payload.title: The note, the hotel bill, and Lestrade's departure

payload.name: Lestrade
payload.note: Lean, ferret-like Scotland Yard detective who works the Boscombe Valley case at Ross; the Lestrade of the Boscombe and Noble Bachelor divisions.

stages.label: Lestrade

quotes.quote: A lean, ferret-like man, furtive and sly-looking
light brown dustcoat and leather-leggings
pea-jacket and cravat, which gave him a decidedly nautical appearance, and he carried a black canvas bag in his hand

stages.text: Lestrade: middle-aged English detective of Scotland Yard; lean, wiry build; pale, weathered skin; thinning sandy hair, close-cropped; narrow, sharp, ferret-like face with furtive, sly eyes and a thin mouth; clean-shaven or with a small moustache. Signature outfit: light brown dustcoat and leather leggings in the country, a navy pea-jacket and cravat in town; a black canvas bag carried in hand.

payload.name: Baker Street lodgings
payload.note: Holmes and Watson's shared rooms in Baker Street, where the client consultation and later supper take place.

stages.label: Baker Street lodgings

quotes.quote: With my body in one easy-chair and my legs upon another
our humble lodging-house mahogany

stages.text: Baker Street lodgings: a sitting room on the first floor of a tall brick terrace in London, with tall sash windows looking onto a narrow street of soot-darkened brick. Mahogany table and sideboard, worn easy-chairs with cushions, a coal fire in a black iron grate, bookshelves and a writing desk stacked with newspapers and papers. Gaslight and lamps, plain papered walls, a few framed prints.

payload.title: The stone's history and the advertisement

payload.name: Baker Street sitting-room
payload.note: Holmes's rooms, where the hat is examined, the stone kept, and the final confrontation takes place.

stages.label: Baker Street sitting-room

quotes.quote: the bright semicircle which was thrown from the fanlight
we were shown up together to Holmes’ room
we were back in the sitting-room at Baker Street

stages.text: Baker Street sitting-room: a first-floor room in a plain brick Baker Street terrace, reached by a steep staircase from the street door beneath a semicircular fanlight. Tall sash windows overlook the street, with heavy curtains. A coal fire burns in a grate beneath a plain mantelpiece; a desk and shelves of papers and books line the walls, with a gasolier overhead.

payload.title: Holmes reads clues from Mary and the letters

payload.name: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes's rooms where the consultations and the final confrontation take place.

stages.label: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street

quotes.quote: his lodgings at Baker Street
we sat on either side of the fire
fly out of that window
a formidable array of bottles and test-tubes
the pungent cleanly smell of hydrochloric acid

stages.text: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street: first-floor rooms in a tall brick Victorian terrace on a busy London street, with a sash window looking over slate roofs and chimney pots. A coal fire burns in the grate beside two armchairs, one deep and worn with a recess beside it. A cluttered desk, shelves of books and newspapers, and a chemistry table of bottles and test-tubes.

payload.title: Holmes's deductions on Watson's marriage

payload.name: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes and Watson's lodgings where the case is discussed and the King visits.

stages.label: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street

quotes.quote: His rooms were brilliantly lit
remained in our lodgings in Baker Street, buried among his old books
I sat down beside the fire

stages.text: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street: a tall brick terraced house in a London street, with a well-kept front door, and upper-floor sitting rooms whose tall sash windows glow with lamplight at dusk. Inside, a coal fire burns in the grate, with a worn carpet, shelves of old books, a desk heaped with papers, and a chemical table by the window.

payload.title: The masked visitor arrives

payload.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, King of Bohemia
payload.note: Hereditary King of Bohemia, visiting London incognito under the name Count Von Kramm; masked client who hires Holmes to recover a photograph of himself with Irene Adler.

stages.label: The King of Bohemia, as Count Von Kramm

quotes.quote: The Count shrugged his broad shoulders.
he tore the mask from his face and hurled it upon the ground
took a heavy chamois leather bag from under his cloak

stages.text: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein: a man in his thirties, broad-shouldered and heavily built; fair skin, short fair hair and a close-trimmed moustache; strong, aristocratic features; a black half-mask hides his eyes and upper face. Signature outfit: a dark wool travelling cloak over a dark frock coat and waistcoat, with a high white collar. Props: a heavy chamois leather bag of gold.

payload.title: Wilson's visit to Holmes

payload.name: Jabez Wilson
payload.note: Stout, florid, red-headed pawnbroker of Saxe-Coburg Square, the client who brings the Red-headed League case to Holmes.

stages.label: Jabez Wilson

quotes.quote: The portly client puffed out his chest with an appearance of some little pride
He wore rather baggy grey shepherd’s check trousers, a not over-clean black frock-coat, unbuttoned in the front, and a drab waistcoat with a heavy brassy Albert chain
there was nothing remarkable about the man save his blazing red head, and the expression of extreme chagrin and discontent upon his features.

stages.text: Jabez Wilson: a stout, pompous pawnbroker of middle age, obese and slow in build, with fair English skin reddened about the face. His hair is a blazing, fiery red, and he has a close-cut red beard. Florid cheeks and a discontented, chagrined expression. Signature outfit: baggy grey shepherd's check trousers, a not over-clean black frock-coat, and a drab waistcoat with a heavy brassy Albert chain and a square pierced metal ornament.

payload.name: Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes's rooms where the opening consultation and the late-night gathering take place.

stages.label: Baker Street rooms

quotes.quote: Two hansoms were standing at the door, and as I entered the passage I heard the sound of voices from above.
as we sat over a glass of whisky and soda in Baker Street

stages.text: Baker Street rooms: a Marylebone street of tall brick terraces with stuccoed fronts, sash windows and iron railings, lamps on iron posts; the rooms lie up a narrow passage and staircase from the street door, with a sitting room of worn furniture, a desk, a coal fire, bookshelves and newspapers.

payload.title: Holmes examines the pawnshop and the bank

payload.name: Saxe-Coburg Square
payload.note: Small shabby square in the City where Wilson's pawnbroker shop stands.

stages.label: Saxe-Coburg Square

quotes.quote: a poky, little, shabby-genteel place, where four lines of dingy two-storied brick houses looked out into a small railed-in enclosure
a lawn of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes made a hard fight against a smoke-laden and uncongenial atmosphere
Three gilt balls and a brown board with “JABEZ WILSON” in white letters, upon a corner house

stages.text: Saxe-Coburg Square: a small, shabby-genteel square in the City of London, near Aldersgate. Four lines of dingy two-storied brick terrace houses face a small railed-in enclosure of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes struggling in smoky air. On a corner house, three gilt pawnbroker's balls and a brown board lettered JABEZ WILSON in white. Gas lamps, worn pavement, soot-stained brick.

payload.name: the main City road near Saxe-Coburg Square
payload.note: Crowded commercial thoroughfare running past the back of Saxe-Coburg Square.

stages.label: Main City road, Victorian commercial thoroughfare
stages.text: The main City road: a wide, busy commercial thoroughfare of grey stone and soot-darkened brick warehouses, banks and shopfronts, with iron gas lamps, tramlines set in cobbles, and tall chimneys in the distance. Plane trees line the pavement in patches, and a few narrow side lanes branch off toward the square.

payload.title: Holmes reads the hat
The whistle and the cry

payload.name: the swamp adder
payload.note: Venomous snake trained by Roylott to crawl down the bell-rope; killed Julia and then Roylott. Seen on stage at the end.

stages.label: the swamp adder

quotes.quote: The speckled band!
The idea of a snake instantly occurred to me
I heard the creature hiss

stages.text: the swamp adder: a venomous Indian snake about four feet long, thick-bodied and muscular, with smooth dry scales in dull yellow-brown ground marked by irregular dark blotches and bands of cream, giving it a speckled look; a broad flattened head with two small dark fangs, and cold watchful eyes.

aliases: the room in which my sister died
payload.name: Helen's bedroom
payload.note: The room where Julia died, with the dummy bell-rope and the ventilator to Roylott's room.

stages.label: Helen's bedroom
stages.text: Helen's bedroom: a plain upper room in a rambling old country house at Stoke Moran, with whitewashed plaster walls, a narrow iron bedstead, a worn wooden floor and a small coal grate. A bell-rope hangs beside the bed, its end lying loose. High on the wall near the bed a ventilator opens into the adjoining room. Tall sash window, heavy curtains.

payload.title: Holmes outlines the case on the train

payload.name: the train to the west
payload.note: Railway journey from Paddington through Reading, Swindon and the Severn valley to Ross.

stages.label: the train to the west

quotes.quote: We had the carriage to ourselves save for an immense litter of papers
he suddenly rolled them all into a gigantic ball and tossed them up onto the rack.
rattling away to Paddington Station.

stages.text: the train to the west: a Great Western compartment carriage of varnished teak panelling, upholstered bench seats in dark green plush, brass luggage racks high above the seats, and framed windows with brass fittings. Beyond the glass, river meadows, hedgerows and the Thames valley slide past.

payload.title: Waiting in the bank cellar

payload.name: Peter Jones
payload.note: Official police agent from Scotland Yard, consequential and brave, who arrests Clay.

stages.label: Peter Jones

quotes.quote: the deeper, heavier in-breath of the bulky Jones
in his consequential way
as brave as a bulldog and as tenacious as a lobster

stages.text: Peter Jones: middle-aged, stout and heavy-set, with a broad, bulky frame and a self-important bearing. Ruddy, weathered skin, close-cropped sandy-grey hair, neat side-whiskers and a clean-shaven upper lip. Heavy, florid features with small, shrewd eyes. Signature outfit: a dark wool frock-coat and waistcoat of charcoal grey, a stiff white collar, and a dark bowler hat. Carries a stout oak truncheon at his belt alone.

payload.name: Mr. Merryweather
payload.note: Long, thin, sad-faced bank director and chairman, who worries about the French gold in the cellar.

stages.label: Mr. Merryweather

quotes.quote: observed Mr. Merryweather gloomily.
the thin, sighing note of the bank director
striking his stick upon the flags

stages.text: Mr. Merryweather: man in his fifties or sixties; tall, long-limbed and thin; pale, drawn, mournful face with deep lines; grey hair and neatly trimmed grey side-whiskers; clean-shaven upper lip. Dark wool frock coat over a waistcoat, high collar and dark cravat, the dress of a bank director; a dark hat. He carries a stout walking stick. Only the stick is his own prop.

payload.name: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank
payload.note: Huge vault beneath the City branch bank where the napoleons are stored and the criminals' tunnel emerges.

stages.label: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank

quotes.quote: We are at present, Doctor—as no doubt you have divined—in the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks.
the cold dank air of the vault
The cellar! There was the end of this tangled clue.

stages.text: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank: a vast low vault of old London brickwork beneath a bank branch in the City, with dank cold air, stone flags underfoot, and a tunnel mouth dug through the wall. Stacked wooden cases of coin stand in rows; gaslight and lantern fittings hang from the arches.

payload.title: The coronet taken home and the son's request

payload.name: Alexander Holder
payload.note: Senior partner of Holder & Stevenson, owner of the Beryl Coronet loan.

stages.label: Alexander Holder

quotes.quote: I am Alexander Holder, of the banking firm of Holder & Stevenson, of Threadneedle Street.

stages.text: Alexander Holder: a man in his late fifties to sixties; solid, portly build; fair complexion gone ruddy; grey hair thinning at the crown and side-parted, with neatly trimmed grey whiskers; a broad, anxious face with heavy brows and kindly eyes. Signature outfit: a dark charcoal wool frock coat over a grey waistcoat, white collar and dark cravat, with a black silk hat. Signature prop: a folded pair of gold-rimmed spectacles he carries in a waistcoat pocket.

payload.name: Arthur Holder
payload.note: Holder's only son, a wild young man in debt; accused of stealing the coronet, actually protecting Mary.

stages.label: Arthur Holder

quotes.quote: He has been a disappointment to me, Mr. Holmes—a grievous disappointment.
I could not bear to see the smile fade even for a moment from his face.

stages.text: Arthur Holder: young man, about twenty-five; slim, fair-haired and clean-shaven, with a ready smile and bright eyes; a pale, fine-boned face. Dressed as a young gentleman of means: a dark wool lounge suit with a white collar and a dark cravat; a grey tweed overcoat when out of doors. Signature props: none.

payload.name: Mary Holder
payload.note: Holder's adopted niece who aids Sir George Burnwell and flees with him.

stages.label: Mary Holder

quotes.quote: Something like fear sprang up in the young lady’s expressive black eyes.
my little Mary, who has a woman’s quick insight into character.

stages.text: Mary Holder: young woman in her early twenties; slender build; fair skin; dark hair worn up in a simple Victorian style; expressive black eyes; delicate, intelligent features. Signature outfit: a dark wool day dress with a fitted bodice and high collar, in deep blue-grey, with a plain shawl. She carries no props.

payload.name: Fairbank
payload.note: Holder's house in Streatham with the dressing-room, hall window and stable lane behind.

stages.label: Fairbank

quotes.quote: Fairbank was a good-sized square house of white stone, standing back a little from the road.
A double carriage-sweep, with a snow-clad lawn, stretched down in front to two large iron gates
On the left ran a lane which led to the stables, and was not itself within the grounds at all

stages.text: Fairbank: a good-sized square house of white stone, standing back from a public road behind a snow-clad lawn. A double carriage-sweep curves to two large iron gates. A narrow path between neat hedges runs from the road to the kitchen door, the tradesmen's entrance, beside a small wooden thicket. A lane to the stables lies outside the grounds behind the house.

payload.title: Helen's fear and the Farintosh reference

payload.name: Helen Stoner
payload.note: Young client, stepdaughter of Dr. Roylott and twin of Julia, who consults Holmes at Baker Street.

stages.label: Helen Stoner

quotes.quote: My name is Helen Stoner, and I am living with my stepfather
covered over her injured wrist
I have been waiting so eagerly for you

stages.text: Helen Stoner: young woman in her twenties; slight build; fair English complexion; fair hair worn up in a plain knot; pale, anxious face with grey eyes; a bruised, injured wrist. Signature outfit: a dark wool travelling dress with a high collar and a plain grey shawl, the colours muted. No props.

payload.name: Baker Street rooms
payload.note: Holmes and Watson's bachelor lodgings where Helen first consults Holmes.

stages.label: Baker Street rooms

quotes.quote: She is waiting now in the sitting-room.
A lady dressed in black and heavily veiled, who had been sitting in the window, rose as we entered.

stages.text: Baker Street rooms: first-floor lodgings in a brick terrace in central London, sooty brick facade, sash windows with lace curtains, a narrow street outside lit by gas lamps and fog. Inside, a sitting-room with a coal fire in a tiled grate, a cluttered desk, bookshelves, newspapers and a bay window overlooking the street.

payload.name: Alice
payload.note: The single protagonist of the book, the young girl who falls down the rabbit-hole and appears in every division; all entries refer to her, and her sister on the bank is not part of this cluster.

stages.label: Alice
stages.text: Alice: a young Victorian English girl of about seven, slight and small-boned, who grows very tall and shrinks very small over the course of her adventures. Skin fair with a light sunburn; long straight light-brown hair that often falls loose into her eyes, which she tosses back with a little shake of her head; bright, eager, curious features. Signature outfit: a plain blue Victorian child's dress with a white pinafore apron, white stockings and buckled shoes. Carries no props of her own.

quotes.quote: that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that _would_ always get into her eyes
Curiouser and curiouser!

payload.name: Alice's sister
payload.note: Alice's unnamed older sister who sits on the riverbank with her, reads a book, and later dreams of Wonderland; both entries are the same individual, so keep them in one cluster.

stages.label: Alice's sister
stages.text: Alice's sister: an older Victorian English young woman, mature but youthful, slender build, fair skin with a faint summer flush, long light-brown hair pinned up loosely with some strands falling about her face, gentle, thoughtful expression. Signature outfit: a pale muslin summer dress with a modest high neckline and long sleeves, in soft cream with a faint sprigged pattern of blue. Signature prop: a small bound book she holds closed in her lap.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee
she sat on, with closed eyes

payload.name: The riverbank
payload.note: The grassy riverbank where Alice sits beside her sister at the start and where the Rabbit runs past; both entries describe this same bank, so they are one place.

stages.label: The riverbank
stages.text: The riverbank: a broad, gently sloping bank of thick summer grass beside a slow river, with a flat open field stretching behind it. A tall, untidy hedge borders the field, and at its base a large rabbit-hole opens in the earth. Old trees stand nearby, shedding dead leaves onto the grass, and a still pool with tall reeds lies close by. Pale, hazy Victorian English countryside under a hot, drowsy sky.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
ran across the field after it
pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge
lying on the bank
the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds

payload.name: The long low hall
payload.note: The single long low hall with locked doors, lamps and a glass table where Alice shrinks and grows; the same hall recurs across divisions, including the later return through the tree-door.

stages.label: The long low hall
stages.text: The long low hall: a long, low passage-hall with a low ceiling from which a row of lamps hangs, lit warmly. Doors line both walls, all locked, with one low curtain concealing a small door about fifteen inches high. Near the middle stands a small three-legged table of solid glass with a slippery surface. Plain panelled walls and a polished stone floor. No people.

quotes.quote: a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof
There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked
a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass
a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high

payload.name: The little door to the garden
aliases: The little door and passage to the garden
payload.note: The small fifteen-inch door in the hall and the passage behind it leading to the garden, reached with the little golden key; the same door is called the garden door and the little golden key door in the later section, so it is one place with both entries.

stages.label: The little door to the garden
stages.text: The little door to the garden: a small door about fifteen inches high, set low in the wall of a long dim hall behind a drawn curtain, with a tiny lock for a little golden key. Beyond it a narrow passage, not much larger than a rat-hole, opens onto a lovely garden of bright flowerbeds and cool fountains. The wood is aged and plain, the frame modest, in a Victorian dream setting.

quotes.quote: behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high
it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole
a low curtain she had not noticed before

payload.name: Bill the Lizard
payload.note: The lizard Bill, sent down the chimney by the Rabbit's servants, kicked out by Alice, then later a juror at the trial who squeaks a pencil and cannot spell stupid; all three entries are the same lizard.

stages.label: Bill the Lizard
stages.text: Bill the Lizard: a small, feeble lizard of modest size, with a long tail, green-scaled and soft-bellied, standing upright on two legs in human posture. Dressed as a Victorian juror in a dark tailcoat, waistcoat and small white cravat, with a slate and pencil. Large, mournful eyes; a thin, wide-mouthed face with a slightly open mouth; small clawed hands; a patient, bewildered demeanour.

quotes.quote: a little feeble, squeaking voice
The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs
the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way
One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked.

payload.name: the guinea-pigs
payload.note: The two guinea-pigs who hold up Bill outside the house and rush at Alice; the same pair later cheering in court and being bagged, so both entries join this cluster and are distinguished only by section.

stages.label: the guinea-pigs
stages.text: the guinea-pigs: a pair of plump, short-eared guinea-pigs drawn as small animals with human posture and dress, standing upright; age: adult; build: round and compact; coat: soft short fur in warm brown and cream patches; facial notes: small dark eyes, rounded snout, whiskers; signature outfit: small period waistcoats and neckcloths in muted green and brown; signature props: a small brown glass bottle carried by one of them.

quotes.quote: being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle
Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court.

payload.name: the Caterpillar
payload.note: The blue hookah-smoking Caterpillar on the mushroom in Wonderland, who questions Alice and gives her advice on the two sides of the mushroom; both entries describe this same individual across divisions.

stages.label: the Caterpillar
stages.text: the Caterpillar: a large blue caterpillar about three inches high, with a segmented, worm-like body, many small legs and folded human-like arms, wearing a simple period waistcoat and a small hat, holding a long hookah pipe. Blue body; its face is calm, heavy-lidded and sleepy.

quotes.quote: a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah
it was exactly three inches high

payload.name: the Pigeon
payload.note: An anxious mother Pigeon in a tree nest who mistakes Alice's long neck for a serpent's and accuses her of hunting eggs.

stages.label: The Pigeon
stages.text: The Pigeon: a large mother pigeon, a bird of middle age with a full, round breast and ruffled grey-and-white feathers, its wings held close and its head pushed forward on a long neck. It is drawn as a bird with human posture and dress, wearing a small shawl about its shoulders and a plain bonnet pinned above its crest. Its eyes are wide and anxious, its beak sharp and slightly open. Its only prop is a small tree-nest it sits upon, woven of twigs and moss.

quotes.quote: “Serpent!” screamed the Pigeon.
I’ve tried the roots of trees, and I’ve tried banks, and I’ve tried hedges
I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time

payload.name: The mushroom clearing
aliases: the open place in the wood
payload.note: The open clearing in the wood where the Caterpillar sits on a large round mushroom and where Alice later nibbles it; the only place described as an open clearing rather than woodland in general.

stages.label: The mushroom clearing
stages.text: The mushroom clearing: an open place in a dreamlike wood, carpeted with grass and long green leaves, with tall trees rising around its edge whose tops are seen from above. At its centre stands a large, perfectly round mushroom, broad enough for a figure to sit upon, with a fat cap and a pale stem. Beyond the open ground the wood thickens into tall trunks and hedges, and a small house about four feet high stands at the clearing's edge.

quotes.quote: as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question
the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: the treetops
payload.note: The high tree where the Pigeon has its nest, among the trees under which Alice had been wandering.

stages.label: the treetops
stages.text: the treetops: the leafy crowns of tall trees in a dream-wood, dense with interlaced branches and foliage, rising high above the ground. The highest tree in the wood stands among them, its uppermost boughs holding a large pigeon's nest. Sunlit leaves and twisting branches, with no people present.

quotes.quote: the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood

payload.name: the open place with the little house
aliases: the little house in the open place
payload.note: An open place with a small house about four feet high, which Alice approaches once she has shrunk to nine inches.

stages.label: the open place with the little house
stages.text: the open place with the little house: a clearing opening in the wood among tall trees, with rough grass and scattered mushroom patches underfoot. In its middle stands a small house about four feet high, built as a modest cottage with a low roof, a narrow door and small windows, of weathered wood or stone with a Victorian storybook charm. Trees and branches ring the clearing, and the surrounding wood is dense and shadowed.

quotes.quote: an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: Cheshire Cat
payload.note: The grinning cat in the kitchen and trees who talks with Alice about the Hatter and the March Hare, and vanishes and reappears; the same grinning cat whose head appears in the air in the croquet-ground scene.

stages.label: Cheshire Cat
stages.text: Cheshire Cat: a large striped cat with a wide, broad grin from ear to ear, long claws and many teeth, drawn as an animal with a sitting posture and a human-like Victorian sense of humour.
