Its body is often absent, leaving only the grin hanging in the air, which fades slowly from the tail end first. Its coat is a soft striped tabby in grey and cream, with a bright pink tongue visible in the grin. It wears no clothing and carries no props.

quotes.quote: a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear
it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin
a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin

payload.name: March Hare
payload.note: The mad anthropomorphic hare of the Mad Tea-Party, one of the three hosts, who offers wine, takes part in the riddles and story-telling, and appears in the Mad Tea-Party division as well as the court scene; the same individual as the March Hare at the tea party. Distinguish from the court-scene and house-scene entries only by identity, since all describe the same hare.

stages.label: March Hare
stages.text: March Hare: an anthropomorphic hare standing upright with human posture and dress, long upright ears, brown-and-tawny fur, adult in age, lean and slightly hunched build, a long muzzle with whiskers, round wide-set eyes, a wild restless look. He wears a rumpled period waistcoat, shirt and tailcoat in muted brown and cream, with a loose cravat and a tall hat tilted askew. He carries a teacup or teapot as his signature prop.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it
It was the _best_ butter,” the March Hare meekly replied.
“Fifteenth,” said the March Hare.

payload.name: Hatter
payload.note: The Mad Hatter of the tea-party and the nervous first witness at the trial are the same individual; the pig-and-pepper mention is the same hatter named only in passing, so all three keys join one cluster.

stages.label: Hatter
stages.text: Hatter: an adult Victorian man of middle years, lean and slightly stooped, with untidy hair in need of cutting and a long pale face. He wears a shabby period waistcoat and frock coat with a tall, battered hat that is sometimes not his own. Colours are faded browns and greys with a dingy cravat. He carries a teacup and a slice of bread-and-butter, and an old pocket watch.

quotes.quote: Your hair wants cutting
He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
he had taken his watch out of his pocket

payload.name: The Duchess's wood
payload.note: The woods around the Duchess's house, where the footmen run out, the pig escapes and the Cat sits in a tree; set near the Duchess's residence, not the mushroom wood.

stages.label: The Duchess's wood
stages.text: The Duchess's wood: a dense woodland of tall shady trees set around the Duchess's house, with a clearing before its front door, broad trunks, low boughs where a cat might sit, and leafy undergrowth under a green canopy; the house stands at the wood's edge and the trees are the place where a footman runs out and a small pig trots away.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her
broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him
trot away quietly into the wood

payload.name: March Hare's House
payload.note: A large house with ear-shaped chimneys and a fur-thatched roof, where the March Hare is said to live; Alice approaches it at the end.

stages.label: March Hare's House
stages.text: March Hare's House: a very large house in a Wonderland wood, its chimneys shaped like ears and its roof thatched with fur. Tall trees and tangled undergrowth surround it, with a clearing of worn ground before the front. No people are present; the house stands alone among the trees and mushrooms of the wood.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
It was so large a house

payload.name: the Dormouse
payload.note: The sleepy dormouse at the Mad Tea-Party between the Hare and the Hatter, who tells the treacle-well story; the same Dormouse appears in the trial chapter, so both entries are one cluster.

stages.label: the Dormouse
stages.text: the Dormouse: a small, drowsy talking dormouse, grey-brown fur with a pale belly, round ears, a thin tail and small whiskers, standing and sitting upright in human posture. Age: adult. Build: slight and plump. Skin: grey-brown fur. Face: small dark eyes that are often shut, a pink nose, long whiskers. Signature outfit: a faded blue waistcoat with a small brass button and a dull green neckcloth. Signature prop: a china teacup held in its small paws.

quotes.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep
he poured a little hot tea upon its nose
I wish you wouldn’t squeeze so

payload.name: Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The short-tempered Queen of Hearts who orders executions, runs the croquet game, sits on the throne at the trial, and appears across the divisions; the one ruler named Queen of Hearts with the Knave's trial and croquet-ground.

stages.label: Queen of Hearts
stages.text: Queen of Hearts: a flat, oblong playing-card royal with a head, arms and legs, drawn as an imperious adult woman of middle age with a stern, frowning face and a commanding bearing. Her hair is dark and bound under a small golden crown. Her skin is fair. Her signature outfit is a long crimson velvet gown with a wide golden-edged collar, trimmed with heart motifs, in deep red and gold. Her signature prop is a rounded golden sceptre held in one hand.

quotes.quote: The Queen turned crimson with fury
ornamented all over with diamonds
the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
frowning like a thunderstorm

payload.name: Tea-table under a tree
aliases: the table in front of the house
payload.note: A large table set out under a tree in front of a house, where the tea-party takes place.

stages.label: Tea-table under a tree
stages.text: Tea-table under a tree: a large wooden table set out in the open under a spreading tree, in front of a house, with a cloth laid across it and many tea-things and cups scattered over its surface. The tree shades the table, with leafy branches and a rough trunk. The house stands behind it with a plain, old-fashioned Victorian front. Ground is level grass before the table.

quotes.quote: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house
The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it
there was nothing on it but tea

payload.name: King of Hearts
payload.note: The mild, timid King who walks in the procession, quietly pardons the condemned players and sits as judge at the trial; distinguished from the Queen by his timidity and pardons.

stages.label: King of Hearts
stages.text: King of Hearts: an elderly, mild, timid man of about sixty with a short grey-white beard and mild anxious face, wearing a tall gold crown set over a great white judge's wig, round spectacles, and a long crimson royal robe with ermine trim over a white waistcoat and knee breeches. Flat oblong playing-card body with head, arms and legs at the corners, decorated with red hearts. Carries a small sceptre in one gloved hand.

quotes.quote: That's the judge, she said to herself, because of his great wig.
as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable
the King put on his spectacles and looked anxiously round
these were ornamented all over with diamonds

payload.name: the Knave of Hearts
payload.note: The Knave of Hearts, a playing card who carries the King's crown in the procession and is later tried for stealing the tarts; the same individual across all three entries, shown carrying the crown, standing accused in chains, and as the cardboard card figure on trial in Alice's dream.

stages.label: the Knave of Hearts
stages.text: the Knave of Hearts: an oblong, flat playing card made of cardboard, with head, arms and legs at the corners, a heart suit ornament on its front, and a plain card-stock finish. Age appears youthful; build slight and flat; skin pale card-white; hair a dark painted brown; face simple, with a bowed, smiling expression. Signature outfit: a red and crimson tunic with a white collar and red breeches. Signature prop: a crimson velvet cushion carrying the King's crown.

quotes.quote: Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion
the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him
being made entirely of cardboard

payload.name: the White Rabbit
payload.note: The single anxious White Rabbit of Wonderland who whispers the Duchess's sentence in the croquet procession and later acts as herald of the court, blowing the trumpet, reading the accusation and calling witnesses; all three entries are the same rabbit across divisions.

stages.label: White Rabbit
stages.text: The White Rabbit: an anxious white rabbit standing upright with human posture, white fur, pink eyes, and long ears, dressed in a waistcoat with a pocket watch. Hurried and nervous in manner, he carries a brass trumpet in one hand and a rolled parchment scroll in the other, and wears round spectacles when reading. Flat, fragile, and precise in his gestures, with a small shrill voice.

quotes.quote: Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner
near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other
The White Rabbit put on his spectacles.

payload.name: the playing-card soldiers
payload.note: The ten oblong card soldiers with clubs who march in the royal procession, form the croquet arches and carry out the Queen's orders in the croquet-ground scenes.

stages.label: the playing-card soldiers
stages.text: the playing-card soldiers: ten flat, oblong card soldiers of the Queen's pack, each with a head, arms and legs at the corners of the card body, carrying a club. Their faces are simple and painted, with stiff moustaches and small pointed hats, dressed in the pack's patterned livery in red and black. Their build is slender and uniform, all identical in size and shape.

quotes.quote: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches

payload.name: the flamingo
payload.note: A live flamingo used as Alice's mallet; it twists its neck and at one point flies off into a tree.

stages.label: the flamingo
stages.text: the flamingo: a live flamingo with long pink-feathered body, slender long legs and a long curving neck, of a size that can be tucked under a girl's arm with its legs hanging down. Its neck is long, flexible and prone to twisting, its plumage pale rose-pink with darker wing edges, and its beak is long and bent downward. It is a bird, not a human, with no clothing or props.

quotes.quote: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down
it _would_ twist itself round and look up in her face

payload.name: the hedgehogs
payload.note: Live hedgehogs used as croquet balls, which roll away and fight one another.

stages.label: the hedgehogs
stages.text: the hedgehogs: small live hedgehogs, each with a rounded body and a coat of brown and fawn spines, short legs, a pointed snout and small dark eyes; in the game they are used as croquet balls, so they are small, round and compact, able to curl into a ball and unroll to crawl away.

quotes.quote: the balls were live hedgehogs
the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away

payload.name: the Queen's croquet-ground
payload.note: The single walled garden croquet-ground of the Queen where the flamingo-and-hedgehog game is played and executions are ordered; both entries describe this same place, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: Queen's croquet-ground
stages.text: Queen's croquet-ground: an enclosed garden of uneven ridges and furrows over lawn, with a few tall trees at its far side and a tall walled border around it. Vegetation is lush green grass and shrubs, with trees behind the walls. Architecture is minimal: a low garden wall and a rounded hedge border, with small painted arches of doubled-up soldiers as hoops. Landmarks are the ridged ground, the scattered arches and the distant trees. Victorian dream-Wonderland setting; no people present.

quotes.quote: it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree
by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left

payload.name: the Gryphon
payload.note: The Gryphon of the Mock Turtle's story and the Lobster Quadrille: a winged creature with an eagle's head and lion's body who guides Alice, interrupts the Mock Turtle, and hurries her to the trial; the same individual as the Gryphon who whispers in the court.

stages.label: the Gryphon
stages.text: The Gryphon: a winged creature with an eagle's head and a lion's body, with wings folded at its back and forepaws. It is a fantastical beast of the Wonderland tradition, drawn in the Victorian illustrated manner of the book, with an eagle's beak and a lion's tawny-gold coat. Its feathers are warm brown and cream, and its wings are large and dark-tipped. No clothing, no props.

quotes.quote: a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun

payload.name: the Mock Turtle
payload.note: Sorrowful calf-headed creature with a turtle's tail who tells of his schooldays in the sea (The Mock Turtle's Story); the same creature who later describes the Lobster Quadrille and sings Beautiful Soup, so both entries belong to this cluster.

stages.label: The Mock Turtle
stages.text: The Mock Turtle: a sorrowful, sobbing sea creature with a calf's head and a turtle's tail, whose body is that of a turtle with a shell and flat flapper-like forelimbs. Its eyes are large and full of tears, and it is stiff and heavy in build, with a deep hollow voice. Its colouring is pale and watery, with a dull grey-green shell, a soft cream underside and a mournful look.

quotes.quote: Once," said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, "I was a real Turtle."
The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes.
sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock

payload.name: Sea-shore
payload.note: The undersea setting where the Lobster Quadrille would be danced along the shore and where the whiting and lobsters are placed.

stages.label: Sea-shore
stages.text: Sea-shore: a wide strip of pale shingle and sand running along the edge of a calm undersea sea, with the open water beyond it, scattered with drifting jelly-fish. Smooth rounded stones, clumps of seaweed and coral outcrops line the shore, and the water fades to deep green-blue further out.

quotes.quote: you first form into a line along the sea-shore
They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance?
when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way
as far out to sea as you can

payload.name: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice
aliases: the court of the Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The single courtroom of the Queen of Hearts where the trial of the Knave takes place; the Lobster Quadrille entry, which only mentions the trial heard in the distance, is the same court and is distinguished only by being unseen on stage.

stages.label: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice
stages.text: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice: a large, crowded courtroom of tall, sombre stone walls and a high roof, with a raised royal throne for the King and Queen of Hearts at one end, a judge's great wig-marked bench, and a jury-box holding twelve jurors writing on slates. In the centre stands a long table bearing a large dish of tarts, and the floor is strewn with a crowd of little birds, beasts and flat playing-card courtiers. Doors lead off to the side, scattered papers litter the floor, and the space is formal and dim.

quotes.quote: the King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne
In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it
she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.

payload.name: the jury
payload.note: The twelve jurors, birds and beasts who write on slates and act together as one body in the court; same jury in both the tart trial and Alice's trial, so the two entries are one cluster.

stages.label: the jury
stages.text: the jury: twelve creatures, a mix of animals and birds, each drawn as an animal or bird with human posture and period dress such as waistcoats and hats; they sit in the jury-box, each holding a slate and pencil. Their forms vary, including a lizard among them. Flat card-like jury members are not used; they are animal and bird figures.

quotes.quote: those twelve creatures, (she was obliged to say "creatures," you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,)
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard)

payload.name: the officers of the court
payload.note: The court officers who suppress the guinea-pigs, remove the Dormouse and attend the Queen's orders in the Hatter's evidence and cook scenes; distinct from the card soldiers who march in the procession.

stages.label: officers of the court
stages.text: the officers of the court: a group of typical members, adult men of middle age, lean and upright, with a stern, dutiful bearing; clean-shaven or with short side whiskers, pale complexion, neat dark hair under a plain low-crowned hat. Each wears a dark formal court coat with high collar over a white shirt and waistcoat, with a brass-buttoned tabard of the Queen's livery in red and gold. They carry a large canvas bag tied with strings and a folded list or scroll.

quotes.quote: They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings
Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!

payload.name: the pack of cards
payload.note: The playing cards of the court who rise up and fly at Alice at the end of the dream; distinct from the jury of birds and beasts.

stages.label: the pack of cards
stages.text: the pack of cards: a group of flat, oblong playing cards of the Queen's court, each card a cardboard figure with a head, arms and legs, painted in the suits of hearts, spades, diamonds and clubs with court-card faces and rich period colours of red, black and gold trim, with plain card backs showing at the edges as they rise.

quotes.quote: being made entirely of cardboard
You’re nothing but a pack of cards!
the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her
